comments.author: @Graybeard_
comments.text: My questions regarding AI robots is who will repair them? How will they be upgraded? If you have robots working at your company, and there is a bearing or seal or something mechanical that prematurely wears out, but the company that manufactured the robots is on the other side of the country, or even in China, logistically, how do you keep operations working? Will there be local certified robot repair shops? With technology racing ahead at break-neck speeds, will your five year old robots be deemed obsolete and not worth repairing/upgrading? What happens to the millions of robots wearing out, breaking or becoming obsolete? I get that creating the AI systems and building robot prototypes is here and now. But where is the infrastructure to repair, maintain and upgrade them? We are still working out EV charging stations and repair shops almost two decades after EVs started appearing on our roads. Since robots are not currently deployed on any scale, and therefore, we lack any experience on how they perform out in the real world, it seems to me we have a huge learning curve still ahead on keeping robots out in the field working efficiently and cost effectively. Will this bearing or piston or servo fail under hot or cold or humid conditions when working 24/7? We can't know these things until we deploy robots in those environments.
